title: Two velocity estimates shared the same ingredient
summary: A simulated association changed sign when the usable comparison set shrank. The algebra explains why the contrast cannot identify a separate physical effect.

sections.heading: Follow the shared input
body: The analysis compared the catalog peak speed v with the relative speed u stored around first passage. The exposure of interest was A = |v − u|. The other discrepancy compared a center-position finite difference with a member-weighted velocity. It also depends on the velocity used to make u.

At fixed v and u, A has only one possible value. A comparison between high and low A at those same exact speeds has no overlap. Coarse bins permit a descriptive comparison but leave some of the speed dependence in place.

sections.heading: What the table shows
body: The published run checked 1,977 simulation rows. The unadjusted high-minus-low contrast was +165.89 km/s. Among 986 rows in coarsened joint bins with both groups, the weighted contrast was −39.28 km/s. Requiring at least two events per group retained 759 rows.
The changing sign and strongly different retention fractions point to a test with independent tracers. These are simulation-derived event rows that can share a host history.

checks.title: Identification and overlap gate
checks.result: The source records the input columns, bin definitions, row counts, derived contrasts and reproduction pseudocode.

next: Compare independently specified tracers at the same snapshot and verify host lineage before assessing whether any model differs.
